instruction: I want to increase my bash command history size to remember more commands. Could you configure the HISTSIZE variable in my shell to store 10000 commands instead of the default?

command: import pyautogui; import time; time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'alt', 't'); time.sleep(0.5)

metadata.explanation: Task requires setting HISTSIZE=10000 in .bashrc to increase command history. Evaluator checks if HISTSIZE=10000 exists in .bashrc. Similar to original - modifying shell configuration variables.

llm_judge_reasons: The grep regex pattern correctly handles leading whitespace with '^[[:space:]]*'
The pattern correctly handles optional 'export' keyword with '(export[[:space:]]+)?'
The pattern correctly handles spaces around the equals sign with '[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*'
The '^' anchor correctly prevents matching commented lines (lines starting with #)
Core verification logic is sound - checking for HISTSIZE=10000 in ~/.bashrc is the correct approach for most users
Minor limitation: only checks ~/.bashrc, not other potential config files like ~/.bash_profile or ~/.profile, but ~/.bashrc is the standard location for interactive shell configuration
Minor edge case: strict '$' anchor means 'HISTSIZE=10000 # comment' would fail, though this is functionally correct
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: To handle trailing comments, consider replacing '$' with '([[:space:]]*#.*)?$' to allow optional trailing comments
For completeness, could check multiple config files with: 'grep -qE ... ~/.bashrc || grep -qE ... ~/.bash_profile || grep -qE ... ~/.profile'
Alternatively, for more robust verification: source the config and check actual variable value with: 'bash -c "source ~/.bashrc && [ \$HISTSIZE -eq 10000 ] && echo 1 || echo 0"'
